Q901.L1t: Under agency and tort law, a business can sometimes be held responsible for harm caused by another party who works on its behalf.
Q901.L2t: The manufacturer supplied nondefective materials, and the installer was a franchisee rather than an employee, so ordinary respondeat superior liability for employees does not apply.
Q901.L3t: The manufacturer knew its logo appeared on the installer's truck and literature, which led the homeowner to reasonably believe the installer was acting for the manufacturer, and a principal who allows such an appearance can be bound as though an agency existed.
Q901.L4t: The manufacturer can be held liable because it let the installer appear to be its agent, so the homeowner has a claim based on apparent agency.
Q901.L2f: A franchise agreement always gives the franchisor full day-to-day control over how the franchisee performs each job, though courts treat that control as irrelevant to liability.
Q901.L3f: The mere existence of a franchise relationship automatically makes the franchisor vicariously liable for the franchisee's negligence, regardless of what the customer saw or believed.
Q901.L4f: The homeowner has a claim against the manufacturer simply because the installer was its franchisee, whether or not any appearance of agency existed.

Q983.L1t: Graves disease is a common cause of thyrotoxicosis and is one of the main autoimmune disorders of the thyroid gland.
Q983.L2t: Graves disease is caused by autoantibodies that stimulate the TSH receptor, producing excess thyroid hormone and usually a diffusely enlarged gland.
Q983.L3t: Graves disease can involve the tissues behind the eye, where autoimmune inflammation and swelling of the extraocular muscles can restrict their movement.
Q983.L4t: Graves disease can cause paralysis or restriction of the eye muscles, which is known as ophthalmoplegia.
Q983.L2f: Graves disease is caused by destruction of thyroid tissue from chronic infection, which leads to underproduction of thyroid hormone.
Q983.L3f: In Graves disease the thyroid enlarges through the growth of many separate autonomously functioning nodules, which is the characteristic finding on examination.
Q983.L4f: Graves disease is characterised by a large multi-nodular goitre, so that is the correct statement.

Q391.L1t: Fatty acids are an important energy source that is stored in adipose tissue as triglycerides and released when the body needs fuel.
Q391.L2t: Free fatty acids are released from adipose tissue by hormone-sensitive lipase during fasting and exercise, and they are carried to tissues such as muscle and heart for oxidation.
Q391.L3t: Free fatty acids are poorly soluble in water, so in plasma they attach noncovalently to the most abundant plasma protein, which is made in the liver.
Q391.L4t: Most free fatty acids travel in the blood attached to the plasma protein albumin.
Q391.L2f: Free fatty acids are released from adipose tissue only after meals, when high insulin levels stimulate triglyceride breakdown.
Q391.L3f: Because free fatty acids need to be shielded from the plasma, they are mostly taken up and carried inside circulating blood cells that deliver them to tissues.
Q391.L4f: Most free fatty acids are carried in the blood inside the red blood cells, so that is the correct answer.
